Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — benchmark BeyondSWE (500 instances, 246 repositories; CrossRepo, DomainFix, DepMigrate, Doc2Repo) and evaluation of models under OpenHands, a search-augmented diagnostic baseline SearchSWE built by the authors, and the Codex harness with two prompts

No SDD approach. Settings: OpenHands scaffold (OpenHands software agent SDK; version Not stated); SearchSWE (authors' extension of OpenHands with web search via SerpAPI/Google and a browser tool via Jina Reader, DeepSeek-V3.2 as summariser; 'not intended as a new agent architecture'); Codex harness v0.118.0 with default prompt and with SearchSWE-style prompt. Models: GPT-5.4 (xhigh in Codex), DeepSeek-V4-Pro (Max), GLM-5, Qwen3.5-Plus, Gemini 3 Pro, Kimi-K2.5, Seed-Coder-2.0, MiniMax-M2.5; appendix: GLM-4.7, DeepSeek-V3.2, Kimi-K2, GPT-5.2, Seed-Coder-1.8, Qwen3-Coder-Plus, Qwen3-235B-A22B

Per instance (benchmark input, not an SDD artefact): problem statement (issue-style for CrossRepo/DomainFix/DepMigrate, rewritten from PRs by an LLM prompt to remove solution details; for Doc2Repo a natural-language repository specification repo_document.md generated by Gemini 3 Pro: purpose, usage examples, public classes and functions, parameters, return types, behaviour, without implementation details or directory structure); Docker environment; test suite (F2P/P2P, or full adapted suite for Doc2Repo). SearchSWE: shared system prompt (search-use policy, local verification) and task-specific user prompts

Not stated as a prescribed development flow. SearchSWE: Phase 1 deep research for coding (iterative reasoning and information seeking with search/browser tools and command execution in the local container) -> Phase 2 rigorous evaluation (patch applied in a fresh container, P2P and F2P tests run)

None in the agent runs (autonomous). Human verification only in benchmark construction: domain experts (DomainFix, three per instance, unanimous), four SE experts (DepMigrate), five senior software engineers and five senior PhD researchers auditing tasks
N/A (no SDD approach); agents run end to end. Doc2Repo exercises repository generation from a specification document

Not classifiable; authors do not use SDD terms (Doc2Repo: 'construct a functional repository from a natural-language specification'; the prompt 'treats the provided specification as the authoritative source')
Both: existing code bases (CrossRepo and DomainFix issue resolution, DepMigrate repository-wide migration) and new projects from an empty workspace (Doc2Repo)

500 instances from 246 repositories: CrossRepo 200 issues / 67 repos (avg 4.1 files, 190.7 lines); DomainFix 72 / 12 repos (4.2 files, 157.6 lines); DepMigrate 178 / 120 repos (8.4 files, 281.6 lines); Doc2Repo 50 repos (26.8 files, 3528.4 lines; about 400 to over 13,000 LOC, 31 of 50 >1,500 lines). Reported average 10.9 files and 1039.6 lines per instance

Python open-source software, mixed; DomainFix covers 11 scientific/engineering fields (astronomy, bioinformatics, computational chemistry, plasma physics, quantum physics, seismology, convex optimization, geospatial, materials science, molecular dynamics, photonic IC design); DepMigrate 23 widely used packages (e.g. Pydantic V1->V2, NumPy 1.x->2.0); Doc2Repo repositories created Jan-Nov 2025 (many MCP servers and LLM tools)

For every configuration: quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors

Project/tasks: 500 BeyondSWE instances in four task families, Docker environments validated by 5 repeated test runs. Configurations: 15 models under OpenHands and SearchSWE (matched pairs), plus Codex + GPT-5.4 with two prompts. Baseline: OpenHands (no search) for SearchSWE; Codex default prompt for the SearchSWE-style prompt. Held constant between OpenHands and SearchSWE: execution environment, editing interface, shell access, test commands, max 200 turns; SearchSWE differs by search/fetch tools and prompts on using retrieved evidence. Acceptance tests: F2P/P2P tests (full adapted suites for Doc2Repo) in a fresh container with test files restored. Repetitions: none stated. Human intervention: none; blocklist prevents access to target repository and solution artefacts

Best overall Codex + GPT-5.4 (xhigh) with SearchSWE-style prompt 56.65 AVG vs 48.48 with default prompt (+8.2; DomainFix +19.4, CrossRepo +8.9; web-search calls about 2.8x). Best OpenHands DeepSeek-V4-Pro 46.12; best SearchSWE DeepSeek-V4-Pro 48.73. SearchSWE improves AVG for 7 of 8 main models (-0.7 to +2.6); of 32 model-task pairs 62.5% improve, 6.2% tie, 31.2% regress; DomainFix gains most, Doc2Repo least. Doc2Repo: at most 2-4 of 50 repositories fully correct. Higher cost or tokens do not reliably give higher AVG. No significance tests

Distinguished settings and models (AVG 9.70-56.65), but SearchSWE effects are small (mostly within ±3 points) and single-run, so their reliability is not shown. Codex comparison changes the prompt, not tool access, so search effect is confounded with prompting. Limitations of the comparison method not stated by the authors beyond describing SearchSWE as 'deliberately simple' and diagnostic

No limitations or threats-to-validity section. Stated gaps: deep search for coding is an open problem; agents must decide which external evidence to trust, ground it in local dependency versions and verify it locally; token productivity rather than volume is the bottleneck; Doc2Repo yields partial functionality without fully correct repositories

Reporting inconsistencies: '10.9 files and 1039.6 lines per instance' (p. 2-3) equals the unweighted mean of the four task-family averages in Table 1, not the per-instance mean (weighted: about 7.9 files and 552 lines); several % Resolved values are not multiples of 1/n of their task (e.g. DomainFix 35.94% and 30.43% with n=72; CrossRepo 43.88% and 41.92% with n=200; DepMigrate 47.13% with n=178), so denominators or exclusions are not reported (Tables 2, 9); abstract calls 46.12 the best OpenHands-based result while SearchSWE (built on OpenHands) reaches 48.73; Figs. 6-7 plot a Kimi-K2-Thinking configuration that is reported in neither Table 2 nor Table 9. Doc2Repo specifications generated by Gemini 3 Pro, which is also an evaluated model. Some reviewers were members of the author team. Cost and token values only in Fig. 7. Data and code: anonymized supplementary material, public links 'will be provided after the review process'. No pre-registration. Programming language: Python
